To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incorporation of sugar palm fiber into cassava starch film improved its physical and thermal properties.

the incorporation of sugar palm fiber (2, 6 and up to 8% w/ of starch) in the cassava starch composite films containing 6% cassava bagasse increased the thickness while decreased the density, water absorption and water solubility.
the addition of SPF to the CS/CBF film significantly influenced its physical and thermal properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the preparation, characterization and evaluation of the properties of a new biocomposite based on cassava starch and sugar palm fiber.
the development of new materials from renewable resources.
the development of a new type of biopolymer composite film based on cassava starch and cassava bagasse reinforced with sugar palm fiber.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SPF is an effective reinforcing agent to enhance the properties of the cassava starch composite films, which is a potential application of SPF in the packaging industry.
the incorporation of 8% w/ w of SPF into the CS/CB matrix could be used for food packaging application.
the addition of SPF improved the mechanical properties and decreased the water sensitivity of CS/CB composite films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hybrid composites could be a promising alternative to conventional packaging materials.
cassava starch films reinforced with sugar palm fiber are promising materials for packaging applications.
the addition of SPF to CS/CB hybrid composites improved its physical and structural properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incorporation of sugar palm fiber into cassava starch films could be used to improve the mechanical properties and water barrier of starch films, and the incorporation of SPF could be used to increase the relative crystallinity of starch films.
the hybrid composite can be used in the development of biodegradable food packaging materials.
the incorporation of sugar palm fiber in cassava starch-based composite films could be a promising strategy for developing biodegradable packaging materials.
